"To assure that the election is determined without taint of fraud or corruption and without irregularities that may have changed the result of an election." UNC Charlotte Political Science Professor Eric Heberlig said the development was a big deal. "It's very unusual for a state board of election not to certify election results," he said. "It's extremely rare." Heberlig said while Friday's election board action is significant, he still thinks Harris will prevail. Heberlig believes the more likely impact is two years down the road when Harris runs for re-election and has to fight off allegations of a tainted election.
